dedupe_keys.name: esa discos database and information system characterising objects in space

description: DISCOS, the Database and Information System Characterising Objects in Space, is the reference database of the European Space Agency's Space Debris Office at ESOC in Darmstadt. It holds more than 40,000 entries for all trackable objects since the start of the space age, with orbital data history, physical properties such as mass, shape and dimensions, launches, launch vehicles and sites, spacecraft, owners, fragmentation events and re-entries; DISCOS 3 introduced an improved data model. Coverage: all catalogued objects worldwide from 1957 to the present, updated continuously. Format and access: the DISCOSweb interface shares objects, fragmentations, re-entries, launchers and launch sites, launches, countries and organisations, and the DISCOSweb API (discosweb-api.sdo.esoc.esa.int) serves object data to programs in JSON; both need a free Space Debris User Account with OpenID Connect sign-in, and use is subject to ESA's terms. Caveats: registration is required; physical properties are estimates for many objects; the API is limited to object information. Simulation uses: equipment specifications and population of satellites for collision risk, re-entry and space weather exposure studies of communication and navigation services. Related records: CelesTrak and Space-Track give orbital elements, and the UCS database gives satellite purposes.
